issues.description: The mimeType request parameter is still reflected unsanitized into the response Content-Type (getMimeType in JolokiaHttpHandler and AgentServlet), a distinct XSS path the official fix closed via MimeTypeUtil sanitization (restrict to application/json or text/plain). Our patch leaves it open.

Invalid callbacks are rejected by throwing IllegalArgumentException from within response-sending rather than being validated early or gracefully stripped (as the official fix does by falling back to plain JSON), which may surface as a 500-style error instead of a clean response.

result.root_cause: Untrusted JSONP `callback` request parameter is concatenated verbatim into a text/javascript response body, so a correct fix must constrain the callback to a safe JavaScript identifier (allowlist) at the sink.
result.summary: Our patch correctly neutralizes the traced callback XSS by validating the callback against an anchored JS-identifier allowlist at every callback sink (servlet and jvm, streaming and non-streaming via IoUtil), so the POV no longer reproduces and the callback attack class is genuinely closed with a sound, non-ReDoS regex. It uses the same defensive strategy as the official fix but is a weaker subset: it omits the mimeType-parameter sanitization (MimeTypeUtil) that the official commit added to close a second XSS vector via the Content-Type header. It also rejects by throwing during response-sending rather than gracefully stripping the callback.
